layers.basics: Fields are vectors defined everywhere; gradient, divergence and curl describe how they change.
layers.deeper: Choose Cartesian, cylindrical or spherical coordinates to match geometry.
layers.expert: Helmholtz theorem: a field is fixed by its divergence and curl plus boundary conditions; Dirac delta for point sources.

layers.basics: Insulators polarise in a field, reducing it by the relative permittivity εr.
layers.deeper: Boundary conditions: tangential E continuous, normal D jumps by surface charge. Method of images and Poisson/Laplace equations solve problems.
layers.expert: D=ε₀E+P=εE; bound charge ρ_b=−∇·P; energy density ½E·D; uniqueness theorem.

layers.basics: Steady currents make magnetic fields; ferromagnetic cores concentrate them.
layers.deeper: B=μH with μ=μ₀μr; ferromagnets show hysteresis and saturation; magnetic circuits use reluctance.
layers.expert: Boundary: normal B continuous, tangential H jumps by surface current. Hysteresis loop area is energy lost per cycle; soft vs hard magnetic materials.

title: Maxwell’s equations
summary: Four equations that govern all electromagnetism.

layers.basics: Gauss’s law for E and B, Faraday’s law and Ampère–Maxwell law describe how charges and currents make fields and how changing fields make each other.
layers.deeper: The displacement current term lets the equations predict waves travelling at c=1/√(μ₀ε₀).
layers.expert: ∇·D=ρ, ∇·B=0, ∇×E=−∂B/∂t, ∇×H=J+∂D/∂t. Boundary conditions and constitutive relations close the system; covariant form F^{μν}.

title: Plane waves and polarisation
summary: Light and radio in free space.

layers.basics: In free space, E and B oscillate perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel at c.
layers.deeper: Polarisation describes the E-field’s orientation: linear, circular or elliptical.
layers.expert: E=E₀e^{j(ωt−kz)}; η₀=√(μ₀/ε₀)≈377 Ω; Poynting S=E×H; in lossy media, skin depth δ=√(2/ωμσ).

layers.basics: When a wave hits a boundary, some reflects and some transmits, with a bend determined by the media’s impedances.
layers.deeper: Reflection coefficient Γ=(η₂−η₁)/(η₂+η₁); Brewster angle gives no reflection for one polarisation; total internal reflection traps light in fibre.
layers.expert: Fresnel equations for TE/TM; phase shifts on reflection; thin-film anti-reflection coatings with quarter-wave layers.

title: Transmission lines
summary: When wires are long compared to wavelength.

layers.basics: When a signal’s wavelength is comparable to wire length, wires act as waveguides with a characteristic impedance.
layers.deeper: Mismatched terminations cause reflections; PCB traces, coax and antennas feeds are transmission lines.

layers.basics: Reflections create standing-wave patterns whose ratio of max to min voltage is VSWR; 1:1 means perfect match.
layers.deeper: VSWR=(1+|Γ|)/(1−|Γ|); high values waste power and can damage transmitters.
layers.expert: Return loss RL=−20log|Γ|; mismatch loss −10log(1−|Γ|²); input impedance of a line Z_in=Z₀(Z_L+jZ₀tanβl)/(Z₀+jZ_L tanβl).

title: Smith chart
summary: A map of impedances and reflections.

layers.basics: The Smith chart is a circular graph that maps complex impedance onto reflection coefficient, making matching problems visual.
layers.deeper: Moving along a line rotates around the centre; adding series and shunt elements moves along circles.
layers.expert: Conformal map Γ=(z−1)/(z+1); admittance chart is a 180° rotation; used for stub and L-network matching and amplifier design.

title: Impedance matching
summary: Make loads look like the line.

layers.basics: Matching networks (L-networks, stubs, quarter-wave transformers) make a load look like the source impedance so power is transferred without reflection.
layers.deeper: Quarter-wave transformer Z_T=√(Z₀Z_L); single-stub tuning; bandwidth shrinks with higher mismatch.
layers.expert: Bode–Fano limit bounds broadband matching; lumped LC L-section Q=√(R_h/R_l−1).

layers.basics: At microwave frequencies, a hollow metal tube guides waves with less loss than coax.
layers.deeper: Modes TE/TM have cutoff frequencies; below cutoff nothing propagates.
layers.expert: Rectangular TE₁₀ cutoff f_c=c/2a; dispersion v_g=c√(1−(f_c/f)²); optical fibre is a dielectric waveguide.

layers.basics: At high frequency, current flows only near the surface of a conductor, raising resistance.
layers.deeper: Skin depth δ=√(2/ωμσ): ~66 µm for copper at 1 MHz; Litz wire and plating mitigate.
layers.expert: R_ac≈R_dc·a/(2δ) for round wire; proximity effect adds in coils; rough surfaces add further loss at GHz.

layers.basics: An antenna turns circuit signals into radiated waves and back; its radiation pattern shows where it sends power.
layers.deeper: Gain is directivity times efficiency; dipole 2.15 dBi; effective aperture A_e=λ²G/4π; Friis equation for links.
layers.expert: Reciprocity; far-field r>2D²/λ; radiation resistance of a half-wave dipole ≈73 Ω; polarisation mismatch loss.

layers.basics: A half-wave dipole is two quarter-wave rods driven at the centre; a monopole above a ground plane acts like half of one.
layers.deeper: Phone antennas are folded and miniaturised variants (PIFA, IFA).
layers.expert: Current distribution sinusoidal; pattern ∝cos(π/2 cosθ)/sinθ; bandwidth depends on thickness; small antennas limited by Chu limit.

layers.basics: Combining several antennas with chosen phases forms a narrow, steerable beam.
layers.deeper: Array factor AF=Σe^{jnψ}; ψ=kd cosθ+β; phased arrays steer electronically without moving.
layers.expert: Grating lobes appear when spacing exceeds λ/2; beamforming weights from DSP; massive MIMO in 5G.

title: EMI/EMC: interference, shielding, grounding
summary: Keeping devices from disturbing each other.

layers.basics: Electronics emit and receive unwanted electromagnetic noise; EMC design ensures devices coexist.
layers.deeper: Shielding, filtering, careful PCB layout (return paths, ground planes) and cable management.
layers.expert: Common-mode vs differential-mode; ferrites; ground loops; ESD (kV transients); FCC/CISPR limits; spread-spectrum clocking.
